task: Draft a data-handling section for a fictional consulting agreement comprising four sub-clauses: (a) purpose limitation, (b) disclosure restriction, (c) security standard, and (d) return and deletion on termination. Use only the supplied facts. Do not add data-retention schedules, breach-notification deadlines, cross-border transfer restrictions, or regulatory citations not in the facts.

facts.text: The fictional consulting agreement is between Paravel Strategies Inc. and Thornton Manufacturing Ltd.
Paravel will process Thornton's confidential data only for the purposes of delivering the consulting services described in the statement of work; it may not use the data for any other purpose.
Paravel will not disclose the data to third parties without Thornton's prior written consent, except where required by applicable law.
Paravel will maintain reasonable technical and organisational measures to protect the data against unauthorised access, loss, or disclosure.
The security standard is described as 'reasonable measures'; no specific framework or certification is required by the agreement.
Upon termination or expiry of the agreement, Paravel will, at Thornton's election, either return all confidential data to Thornton or certify in writing that it has securely deleted the data.
The return-or-delete obligation applies within 30 days of termination or expiry.
The facts do not specify a data-retention period before termination.

forbidden_additions: A specific security framework or certification requirement not in the facts.
A breach-notification timeline or incident-response procedure.
A cross-border transfer restriction or reference to a specific privacy regulation.
preserve: The purpose limitation tied to the statement of work.
The written-consent requirement for third-party disclosure, with the law-required exception.
The 'reasonable measures' security standard without elevating it to a named framework.
The 30-day return-or-delete obligation at Thornton's election on termination.
